memory_leads.lead: A nominal seafarer employment contract does not by itself describe effective freedom of choice. Recruitment debt, withheld pay, control over documents, practical barriers to leaving and fear of retaliation can create a different person-level mobility and bargaining state without this Memory pass making any forced-labor or trafficking finding.

Recruitment intermediation can be multi-layered. A seafarer may encounter a licensed or known crewing organization, local subagents, informal brokers, training/medical intermediaries or lenders, so the party collecting money or making promises may differ from the ultimate employer or principal.

Recruitment-fee or debt exposure is a pre-boarding financial state rather than proof of abuse. Borrowing, family financing, broker charges or bundled preparation costs can change the worker's downside from quitting, complaining or returning early; exact legality, amount and responsibility require Evidence.

Contract expectation and onboard reality can diverge. Job, vessel, wage, duration, deduction, leave or working-condition terms remembered or represented before joining may differ from documents or practice later encountered; the structural state is mismatch/substitution, not a legal conclusion about breach or deception.

Wage delay, partial payment, unexplained deductions and withholding are distinct cash-flow states. Even when ultimate entitlement is unresolved, delayed access to expected earnings can increase household debt, reduce remittances and make early exit financially harder.

Possession of identity or travel documents and practical access to them are different from document validity. Documents may be stored for administrative or security reasons, but a seafarer's ability to retrieve and use them when needed is a separate mobility state whose exact legality depends on context.

Exit capability is a chain rather than a resignation flag. Notice/permission expectations, wage or debt concerns, document access, port access, immigration/travel gates, replacement logistics and fear of consequences can all affect whether a person can practically terminate and return home.

Threat, intimidation or retaliation risk can suppress reporting before any formal grievance exists. The relevant Memory state is perceived consequence for complaining, refusing work, seeking medical help, contacting family/support or attempting to leave; exact allegations and actor intent require Evidence.

Work/rest interference can interact with dependency. Long or irregular hours, understaffing, repeated call-outs or pressure not to record/report problems may increase fatigue and reduce the practical capacity to seek help, while exact work-hour violations remain Evidence questions.

Isolation can amplify dependency. Limited connectivity, remote anchorage/port access, language barriers, unfamiliar jurisdictions and weak peer networks can make external support harder to reach even when formal complaint channels nominally exist.

A grievance channel has multiple usability states: awareness, access, confidentiality, ability to communicate outside the immediate chain of command, perceived non-retaliation, acknowledgement, investigation/response and follow-up. Presence of a procedure alone does not establish effective remedy.

Remediation can require several independent outcomes: immediate safety/welfare support, restored document access, wage-account reconciliation, relief/repatriation, debt or fee dispute handling, replacement employment support and referral to appropriate authorities or services. Exact remedies and liability are not inferred here.

Labor exploitation risk can distort effective labor supply. A nominally staffed vessel may rely on workers whose ability to refuse, report or leave is constrained, so headcount and signed contracts can overstate the resilience and voluntariness of the labor system without proving any specific legal classification.

P033 recruitment/employment is refined by separating ordinary recruitment and contract administration from dependency or coercion-risk states. The same formal joining process can produce very different worker agency depending on debt, information accuracy, payment and exit conditions.

P034 grievance/labor-relations states are refined because an individual grievance mechanism may be practically unusable when confidentiality, retaliation fear, language, connectivity or access to independent support are weak, even without collective industrial action.

P039 crew mobility is refined by distinguishing legal/travel admissibility from practical worker-controlled mobility. Valid documents and an available itinerary do not guarantee a person feels or is practically able to leave an employment situation.

P042 household financial protection is refined because recruitment debt or wage withholding can create household vulnerability before any injury/compensation event, making labor conditions and family cash flow part of the same broader resilience picture.

Generic fatigue, connectivity and household-welfare mechanisms are already present in P032/P038/P042; P043 adds how those states can interact with dependency, reporting and exit constraints rather than repeating the underlying mechanisms.

Memory-not-Evidence, known-time and claim-scoped authority are already Baseline semantics; P043 applies them to recruitment promises, pay records, document access, complaints and remediation without making misconduct findings.

reviewed_no_specific_memory.reason: A legal classification depends on authoritative definitions, facts and context. Blind Memory retains risk-state vocabulary only and makes no forced-labor, trafficking or criminal finding.
Individual allegations, actors, victim status, causation, findings, remedies and chronology require claim-scoped Evidence and should not be reconstructed from blind Memory.
Provider/actor identity, conduct and capability become organization-specific claims requiring Evidence; this pass is not a blacklist or provider directory.
Current legal duties, enforcement practice and remedies are time-sensitive jurisdictional claims requiring source-first authoritative material.

stop_reason: The exploitation-risk chain is populated from recruitment intermediation and fee/debt exposure through contract mismatch, wage access, document control, practical exit capability, retaliation/reporting, work/rest dependency, grievance usability and multi-part remediation. Further recall becomes legal-definition-, victim/case-, actor-, remedy-, enforcement- or jurisdiction-specific.
truth_boundary: Memory-only orientation; no forced-labor, trafficking, coercion, wage-theft, document-retention violation, recruitment-fee violation, actor misconduct, victim status, remedy entitlement, legal threshold or jurisdiction-specific rule is verified.
